       Do one quiz at a time, without looking at the key.
       Target:

       to the next course.
       Mark your score at the top of each quiz. If you score under 9, review that course, then retake it.
       Print pages 2-9 for the quizzes only. The Answer Key starts after a clear page break, so you can print it separately
       or leave it out.

Quiz 1 - Vehicle Servicing and Safety Checks                              Name: __________________ Date: __________


Score: ___ / 10 Target: 9 / 10 before moving on


  Modules Covered
  1. High Voltage Awareness | 2. Best Practice Vehicle Servicing | 3. Best Practice Vehicle Safety Checks


1. How are high-voltage cables on a hybrid or electric vehicle usually identified? [High Voltage Awareness]
    A. Blue insulation
    B. Orange insulation or orange conduit
    C. Green insulation
    D. Plain black insulation with no marking

2. What must be done before working near a high-voltage system? [High Voltage Awareness]
    A. Just switch the ignition off and start work
    B. Rev the engine to discharge the battery
    C. Follow the manufacturer isolation procedure, wear rated PPE, and verify the system is powered down
    D. Disconnect the 12-volt battery only, with no other checks

3. Which gloves are required for high-voltage work? [High Voltage Awareness]
    A. Ordinary disposable workshop gloves
    B. Electrically insulated gloves of the correct class, checked and in test date, with leather protectors
    C. Heat-resistant welding gloves
    D. No gloves, so you can feel components better

4. Why should servicing follow the manufacturer schedule and specification? [Best Practice Vehicle Servicing]
    A. It is only needed to keep a service stamp in the book
    B. Any parts and fluids will do if they look similar
    C. It keeps the vehicle safe and reliable and protects warranty, using the correct parts, fluids, and intervals
    D. It lets you skip items that look clean

5. When lifting a vehicle for servicing, you should: [Best Practice Vehicle Servicing]
    A. Lift on any flat part of the floor pan
    B. Use the manufacturer lifting points, check the lift is secure, and use stands where required
    C. Work under a vehicle supported only by a jack
    D. Lift as fast as possible to save time




Quiz 1 - Vehicle Servicing and Safety Checks (1 of 2)                                                          Practice Material
Quiz 1 - Vehicle Servicing and Safety Checks (continued)                                                   Score: ___ / 10


6. Before returning a serviced vehicle, the final checks should include: [Best Practice Vehicle Servicing]
    A. Only washing the vehicle
    B. Fluid levels, leaks, wheel nut torque, warning lights, and a road test where required
    C. Resetting the trip meter only
    D. Nothing, if no fault was reported

7. A brake safety check should include: [Best Practice Vehicle Safety Checks]
    A. Pedal feel and travel, fluid level and condition, pad and disc condition, and hoses and lines for leaks or
    damage
    B. Only whether the brake lights work
    C. Only the handbrake holding on a hill
    D. Only a visual look through the wheel spokes

8. A tyre safety check should include: [Best Practice Vehicle Safety Checks]
    A. Colour and brand only
    B. Tread depth, pressures, cuts, bulges, uneven wear, and age or damage
    C. Only whether the tyre holds air
    D. Only the spare tyre

9. During a safety check, lights and signalling should be checked for: [Best Practice Vehicle Safety Checks]
    A. Brightness only
    B. Operation of all lamps, indicators, brake lights, and the horn, plus lens damage
    C. Headlamp aim only, with no bulb check
    D. Nothing if the vehicle passed last time

10. If a safety check finds a safety-critical defect, you should: [Best Practice Vehicle Safety Checks]
    A. Ignore it if the customer is in a hurry
    B. Clear it without recording it
    C. Record it clearly, report it, and advise that the vehicle should not be used until it is repaired
    D. Mention it only if the customer asks


   Finished? Score yourself from the Answer Key at the back. Target 9 / 10 before moving on. Note any module to
   review: ________________________________________




Quiz 1 - Vehicle Servicing and Safety Checks (2 of 2)                                                      Practice Material
Quiz 2 - Cooling System Servicing                                         Name: __________________ Date: __________


Score: ___ / 10 Target: 9 / 10 before moving on


  Modules Covered
  1. Understanding Engine Coolants | 2. Engine Coolant Testing | 3. Best Practice Coolant Drain and Flush | 4.
  Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Diagnostics | 5. Drive Belt Diagnostics


1. What does engine coolant do besides preventing freezing? [Understanding Engine Coolants]
    A. It raises the boiling point and contains corrosion inhibitors that protect the engine and radiator
    B. It lubricates the water pump bearings only
    C. It cleans the engine oil
    D. Nothing - plain water does the same job in all conditions

2. Why should different coolant types (for example OAT and older IAT types) generally not be mixed?
[Understanding Engine Coolants]

    A. Mixing changes the colour only, with no other effect
    B. The additives can react, reducing corrosion protection and forming deposits or gel
    C. Mixing makes the coolant freeze-proof forever
    D. Mixing is required at every service

3. Which tool measures coolant freezing protection by how much the coolant bends light? [Engine Coolant
Testing]

    A. A multimeter
    B. A refractometer
    C. A torque wrench
    D. A stethoscope

4. Coolant test strips are mainly used to check: [Engine Coolant Testing]
    A. Tyre pressure and tread depth
    B. Freeze protection, pH, and the remaining corrosion-inhibitor level
    C. Engine oil viscosity
    D. Battery voltage

5. Best practice when draining and flushing a cooling system includes: [Best Practice Coolant Drain and Flush]
    A. Opening the cap on a hot engine to drain faster
    B. Pouring old coolant down a drain
    C. Working on a cold engine, catching and disposing of old coolant correctly, flushing as directed, and refilling
    with the correct coolant
    D. Refilling with plain water only




Quiz 2 - Cooling System Servicing (1 of 2)                                                                  Practice Material
Quiz 2 - Cooling System Servicing (continued)                                                            Score: ___ / 10


6. After refilling a cooling system, why must air be bled out correctly? [Best Practice Coolant Drain and Flush]
    A. Air pockets can cause overheating, poor heater output, and false temperature readings
    B. Air improves cooling, so it should be left in
    C. Bleeding is only done for appearance
    D. Air pockets only affect the air conditioning

7. Most engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensors are NTC thermistors. This means their resistance: [Engine
Coolant Temperature Sensor Diagnostics]
    A. Rises as temperature rises
    B. Falls as temperature rises
    C. Never changes
    D. Is always zero

8. An ECT sensor circuit reads a very cold temperature on a fully warmed engine. A likely cause is: [Engine
Coolant Temperature Sensor Diagnostics]

    A. A perfect sensor
    B. Low tyre pressure
    C. An open circuit or high resistance in the sensor or its wiring, keeping the signal voltage high
    D. A new thermostat

9. A drive belt should be replaced if inspection shows: [Drive Belt Diagnostics]
    A. Cracks, glazing, fraying, chunking, or contamination with oil or coolant
    B. Only a little dust on the surface
    C. The printed brand name has faded
    D. Nothing - belts last the life of the vehicle

10. A belt squeal on start-up most often points to: [Drive Belt Diagnostics]
    A. A faulty spark plug
    B. Low fuel level
    C. A worn or glazed belt, weak tensioner, or pulley misalignment slipping under load
    D. Worn brake pads


   Finished? Score yourself from the Answer Key at the back. Target 9 / 10 before moving on. Note any module to
   review: ________________________________________




Quiz 2 - Cooling System Servicing (2 of 2)                                                               Practice Material
Quiz 3 - Engine Oil Essentials                                                 Name: __________________ Date: __________


Score: ___ / 10 Target: 9 / 10 before moving on


   Modules Covered
   1. Oil Filterization Principles | 2. Engine Oil Velocity and Performance Classifications | 3. Engine Oil Basis Additives
   and Compositions | 4. Engine Oil Synthetic Versus Mineral | 5. Engine Oil Selections


1. What is the job of the bypass valve in an oil filter? [Oil Filterization Principles]
    A. To stop all oil flow when the filter is new
    B. To let oil bypass a blocked filter so the engine still gets oil, even if it is unfiltered
    C. To increase oil pressure at idle only
    D. To drain oil back to the sump overnight

2. What does the anti-drainback valve in a filter prevent? [Oil Filterization Principles]
    A. Oil draining out of the filter and galleries when the engine is off, which would delay oil pressure on start-up
    B. Fuel entering the oil
    C. Coolant mixing with oil
    D. Oil being filtered too well

3. On a 5W-30 oil, what does the "5W" describe? [Engine Oil Velocity and Performance Classifications]
    A. The oil's fuel economy rating
    B. Its cold-temperature (winter) viscosity rating - how it flows when cold
    C. The size of the container
    D. The oil change interval in weeks

4. Performance classifications such as API and ACEA categories tell you: [Engine Oil Velocity and Performance
Classifications]

    A. Only the colour of the oil
    B. Whether the oil meets the required performance level for that engine type and emissions equipment
    C. That any oil with a higher price is approved
    D. Nothing - viscosity grade is the only thing that matters

5. What do detergent and dispersant additives in engine oil do? [Engine Oil Basis Additives and Compositions]
    A. Make the oil foam on purpose
    B. Wash the outside of the engine
    C. Detergents clean deposits from surfaces and dispersants keep particles suspended so the filter can remove
    them
    D. Replace the need for an oil filter




Quiz 3 - Engine Oil Essentials (1 of 2)                                                                        Practice Material
Quiz 3 - Engine Oil Essentials (continued)                                                                 Score: ___ / 10


6. Anti-wear additives such as ZDDP protect the engine mainly by: [Engine Oil Basis Additives and Compositions]
    A. Thickening the oil when hot
    B. Forming a protective film on metal surfaces where the oil film is thinnest, such as cam lobes
    C. Cooling the coolant
    D. Sealing tyre punctures

7. Compared with mineral oil, synthetic oil generally offers: [Engine Oil Synthetic Versus Mineral]
    A. Worse cold starting flow
    B. More uniform molecules, better cold flow, and better resistance to heat and oxidation
    C. No difference at all
    D. A shorter life in every engine

8. Which statement about mineral oil is correct? [Engine Oil Synthetic Versus Mineral]
    A. It is made in a laboratory with no crude oil involved in any grade
    B. It never needs changing
    C. It is refined from crude oil, costs less, and can be suitable where the manufacturer specifies it
    D. It is always better than synthetic at high temperature

9. When selecting engine oil for a service, the deciding source is: [Engine Oil Selections]
    A. Whatever oil is already open in the workshop
    B. The manufacturer specification - viscosity grade and approval / performance category for that engine
    C. The colour of the old oil
    D. The cheapest oil on the shelf

10. A vehicle used mainly for short trips should have its oil: [Engine Oil Selections]
    A. Changed less often, because the engine does fewer miles
    B. Never changed if the level looks full
    C. Topped up with any grade available
    D. Changed on the severe-service schedule, because short trips cause moisture and fuel contamination and the
    oil rarely gets fully hot


   Finished? Score yourself from the Answer Key at the back. Target 9 / 10 before moving on. Note any module to
   review: ________________________________________

Quiz 4 - Transmission Servicing                                          Name: __________________ Date: __________


Score: ___ / 10 Target: 9 / 10 before moving on


  Modules Covered
  1. Six Speed Hydramatic Services | 2. Mercedes-Benz Seven Seven Point Nine Transmission Service | 3. VW Audi
  DSG Service | 4. VF Four Horsepower 16 Transmission Service Checks


1. Why must the correct specified fluid be used in a 6-speed Hydramatic automatic? [Six Speed Hydramatic
Services]

    A. Any automatic fluid shifts the same way
    B. Friction characteristics are matched to the clutches and shift calibration - the wrong fluid can cause harsh or
    slipping shifts
    C. Fluid type only affects the colour in the pan
    D. The fluid is only there to cool the casing

2. On many modern automatics with no dipstick, fluid level is checked by: [Six Speed Hydramatic Services]
    A. Guessing from the amount drained out
    B. Removing the wheels
    C. Bringing the fluid to a specified temperature and checking flow from the level / overflow plug as directed
    D. Overfilling, then driving until the excess escapes

3. A Hydramatic pan service should include: [Six Speed Hydramatic Services]
    A. Reusing the old fluid to save cost
    B. Inspecting the pan and magnet for debris, fitting a new filter and gasket where specified, and refilling with fresh
    specified fluid
    C. Tightening pan bolts as tight as possible in any order
    D. Skipping the filter if the fluid looks clean

4. The Mercedes-Benz 722.9 (7G-Tronic) transmission fluid level is set by: [Mercedes-Benz Seven Seven Point Nine
Transmission Service]

    A. A conventional dipstick at any temperature
    B. Filling until fluid pours out cold
    C. Guesswork based on road feel
    D. The overflow method at a specified fluid temperature, using only the approved-specification fluid

5. Why is using only the approved fluid specification critical on the 722.9 service? [Mercedes-Benz Seven Seven
Point Nine Transmission Service]

    A. Unapproved fluid can upset shift quality and clutch friction and may damage the transmission
    B. It only changes the service invoice wording
    C. Any red automatic fluid is identical
    D. Approved fluid is only needed under warranty for paperwork




Quiz 4 - Transmission Servicing (1 of 2)                                                                   Practice Material
Quiz 4 - Transmission Servicing (continued)                                                                Score: ___ / 10


6. Debris on the pan magnet or in the filter during a transmission service tells you: [Mercedes-Benz Seven Seven
Point Nine Transmission Service]

    A. Nothing - it should always be ignored
    B. To add more fluid and return the vehicle
    C. About internal wear - heavy friction material or metal can point to clutch or component wear that needs further
    diagnosis
    D. That the fluid was overfilled at the factory

7. On a wet-clutch VW / Audi DSG, routine service centres on: [VW Audi DSG Service]
    A. Changing the DSG fluid and filter at the specified interval, because the fluid cools and operates the clutches
    and mechatronics
    B. Never changing the fluid - it is sealed for life in all versions
    C. Adjusting a clutch cable
    D. Replacing the torque converter

8. How is a DSG different from a conventional automatic? [VW Audi DSG Service]
    A. It has no gears at all
    B. It uses two clutches and two gear sets, preselecting the next gear for very fast shifts, and has no torque
    converter in most versions
    C. It is a manual gearbox with no electronics
    D. It only works in reverse

9. Transmission service checks on the ZF-type unit in this course should include: [VF Four Horsepower 16
Transmission Service Checks]

    A. Only a wash of the casing
    B. Fluid level and condition, leaks, fault-code scan, cooler lines, and a road test of shift quality
    C. Removing the transmission for every service
    D. Checking only the engine oil

10. Burnt-smelling, dark transmission fluid found during service checks most likely indicates: [VF Four
Horsepower 16 Transmission Service Checks]

    A. Normal fluid that needs no action
    B. Too much coolant in the system
    C. A recently changed filter
    D. Overheating and clutch wear - the cause should be diagnosed, not just the fluid changed and returned


   Finished? Score yourself from the Answer Key at the back. Target 9 / 10 before moving on. Note any module to

Answer Key - Quiz 1: Vehicle Servicing and Safety Checks

Retake date: ____________________           Second score: ___ / 10

1. B - High-voltage cables and connectors are identified by orange insulation or conduit.

2. C - Isolate and power down following the manufacturer procedure, wear rated PPE, and verify the system is safe
before work.

3. B - Electrically insulated gloves of the correct class, in test date, with leather over-gloves for protection.

4. C - The manufacturer schedule uses the correct parts, fluids, and intervals, keeping the vehicle safe and protecting
warranty.

5. B - Use the specified lifting points, confirm the lift is secure, and use stands where required. Never rely on a jack
alone.

6. B - Final checks cover fluid levels, leaks, wheel nut torque, warning lights, and a road test where required.

7. A - A brake check covers pedal feel, fluid, pads and discs, and hoses and lines for leaks or damage.

8. B - Check tread depth, pressures, cuts, bulges, uneven wear, and age or damage - including the spare where
fitted.

9. B - All lamps, indicators, brake lights, and the horn must work, with no lens damage affecting output.

10. C - Record and report safety-critical defects clearly and advise the vehicle should not be used until repaired.




Answer Key - Quiz 1                                                                                           Practice Material
Answer Key - Quiz 2: Cooling System Servicing

Retake date: ____________________          Second score: ___ / 10

1. A - Coolant raises the boiling point, lowers the freezing point, and carries corrosion inhibitors.

2. B - Mixing different additive types can reduce protection and form deposits or gel. Use the specified type.

3. B - A refractometer measures freeze protection from how the coolant bends light.

4. B - Test strips check freeze protection, pH, and remaining inhibitor (reserve alkalinity) level.

5. C - Work cold, catch and dispose of old coolant correctly, flush as directed, and refill with the correct coolant and
mix.

6. A - Trapped air causes overheating, poor heater output, and false temperature readings, so bleeding matters.

7. B - An NTC sensor's resistance falls as temperature rises.

8. C - An open or high-resistance circuit keeps signal voltage high, which the control unit reads as very cold.

9. A - Cracks, glazing, fraying, chunking, or oil/coolant contamination all mean the belt should be replaced.

10. C - Start-up squeal usually means the belt is slipping: worn or glazed belt, weak tensioner, or misalignment.




Answer Key - Quiz 2                                                                                        Practice Material
Answer Key - Quiz 3: Engine Oil Essentials

Retake date: ____________________          Second score: ___ / 10

1. B - The bypass valve opens if the filter blocks, so the engine still receives oil rather than none.

2. A - The anti-drainback valve keeps oil in the filter and galleries when off, giving faster pressure on start-up.

3. B - The number before W is the winter (cold) viscosity rating; 30 is the hot viscosity grade in 5W-30.

4. B - API / ACEA categories confirm the oil meets the performance level that engine and its emissions equipment
require.

5. C - Detergents clean surfaces; dispersants keep particles in suspension so the filter can trap them.

6. B - Anti-wear additives form a protective film on loaded metal surfaces where the oil film is thinnest.

7. B - Synthetic oil has more uniform molecules, with better cold flow and heat / oxidation resistance.

8. C - Mineral oil is refined from crude, costs less, and is suitable where the manufacturer specifies it.

9. B - Always select by the manufacturer specification: viscosity grade plus the required approval / category.

10. D - Short trips contaminate oil with moisture and fuel and rarely get it fully hot - use the severe-service interval.




Answer Key - Quiz 3                                                                                          Practice Material
Answer Key - Quiz 4: Transmission Servicing

Retake date: ____________________          Second score: ___ / 10

1. B - Fluid friction characteristics are matched to the clutches and shift calibration; wrong fluid causes shift faults.

2. C - With no dipstick, level is set at a specified fluid temperature using the level / overflow plug procedure.

3. B - Inspect pan and magnet, renew filter and gasket where specified, and refill with fresh specified fluid.

4. D - The 722.9 level is set by the overflow method at a specified temperature with approved-specification fluid only.

5. A - Unapproved fluid can upset friction and shift quality and may damage the transmission.

6. C - Heavy debris signals internal wear and needs further diagnosis, not just a fluid change.

7. A - Wet-clutch DSG fluid cools and operates the clutches and mechatronics, so fluid and filter changes are
scheduled service items.

8. B - A DSG uses two clutches and two gear sets, preselecting the next gear, with no torque converter in most
versions.

9. B - Service checks cover fluid level and condition, leaks, fault codes, cooler lines, and shift quality on road test.

10. D - Burnt, dark fluid points to overheating and clutch wear; find the cause instead of only changing the fluid.
